surfaces.part: terrain tile (dark teal water with sand/wood-tone strip along left edge)

answer.evidence: The candidate is a full 16x16 opaque terrain autotile: a tan sand strip on the left columns and dark teal water filling the rest. The column scans show one uniform run over rows 0-15 with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or roof plane. It is flat ground-like terrain with no standing volume and no separate front face, so it reads as a flat top-down tile, which is expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a single small, mostly uniform dark teal block with a thin brown strip on its left edge. It does not read as a 4x3 sand patch with a mask edge. By eye I can only make out about 3 tones: a base fill, one slightly darker area and the edge strip. I see no grain, speckle, sand dots or per-pixel variation. The reference grass has tufts and mottling in several greens, and the paving has stones shaded one by one. The measured facts (10 visible tones, 20% near-flat) are better than my reading of the picture, but the large uniform areas and the lack of visible grain keep it below the references. There is no clear dark outline, since forms are separated only by the edge strip, and the 0% near-neutral edge share means no black sticker line. With so little structure and texture showing, and the rule to fail when in doubt, it fails.

answer.evidence: The tile fills the full 16x16 square (width 16 on every row, with no transparent rows). The column scans show a uniform dark teal across rows 0-15 at x=4, 8 and 11.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a tiny dark teal square (about 14x14 source px) with a brownish edge on its left side, not a 4x3 tile sand patch. The 10 visible tones per tile look generous next to the grass reference's 3, but the whole piece has only 10 distinct colours against 80 in the grass reference. The patch reads as a nearly uniform dark teal block with little visible grain or clumping, so I see about 3 shading steps against the references' 5 or more. At this size it is not comparable to the grass or paving references, which carry per-pixel grain and tufts or stone-by-stone shading, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
